text: The migration has been tested end to end. But right now, only one person knows how any of it actually works. This lesson writes that knowledge down before it becomes a problem.

If Theo is out sick during launch week, or isn't the one who gets paged at 2 a.m., that knowledge needs to already exist somewhere Priya or a teammate can find it. A migration that only lives in one person's head isn't actually done -- it's undocumented risk with a deadline attached.

A short, practical runbook covers five things: a resource inventory table of everything created, where the images live now and the URL pattern the app builds, how to reach the VM and where the app's service definition lives, what the alert watches and who it notifies, and the known limitations -- restating the scope so nobody assumes capabilities that were never built.

A simple table -- resource group, storage account, container and tier, VM name and size, workspace, alert, action group -- answers most of "what exists and where" without anyone running a single CLI command first.

This comes before the cutover presentation on purpose. A presentation built on documentation that doesn't exist yet is built on sand -- and "write it up after launch" is exactly when nobody has time to.
With the runbook written, next lesson presents the actual go-live plan to Priya, built on top of everything documented here.
